summary.intent: Use the GSD workflow (/gsd-plan-phase then /gsd-execute-phase) to plan and then execute Phase 69 — a large Rust port adding FUSE/WinFsp integration with grant-root awareness — including research, validation, pattern-mapping, planning, plan verification, and wave-based parallel execution with worktree isolation.
summary.outcome: Planning completed successfully: 14 plans across 7 waves were researched, written, verified, and committed (surviving a mid-run planner crash via a scheduled resume). Execution then proceeded through waves 1-4 (9 of 14 plans merged, all cargo-green) until plan 69-09 uncovered a genuine architectural gap — the FUSE write path was never migrated off legacy ECIES-wrapped data, making the planned read-path cutover unsafe — so the orchestrator merged the one remaining independent plan (69-11) and halted the FUSE cutover pending a human replanning decision.

repo: The GSD commit helper reports false-negative `commit_failed` even when the commit and lint-staged hooks succeeded — always verify via `git log`/`git status` before retrying.
API-SURFACE regeneration (intel hook) is TS/JS-focused and returns `symbolCount: 0, stale: true` for Rust-only phases — expected, not an error.

`SentShareResponseDto` (apps/api/src/shares/dto/share-response.dto.ts) has no `revoked`/status field since shares are hard-deleted on revoke, so every row from `GET /shares/sent` is inherently an active grant.
The actual GitHub Actions workflow name is "Desktop E2E Tests", not "CI E2E Tests" as ROADMAP.md/CONTEXT.md word it — using the wrong name in `gh workflow run` would 404.
`crates/core`'s `build_node_aad` fail-closes on non-UUID node IDs, so Rust test fixtures across multiple plans (69-04, 69-06, 69-08) needed real UUIDv5 strings, not arbitrary test strings.
Fresh git worktrees lack `node_modules`, so the first commit in a worktree-isolated executor agent fails husky's `lint-staged` step until `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` is run.

The FUSE write path (`crates/fuse/src/write_ops/implementation/{mkdir,upload,delete,rename}.rs`) was never migrated to produce Node-v3/`SealedChildRef`-shaped (symmetric) data — it still emits legacy ECIES-wrapped output, so there is nothing symmetric for a read-path swap to unwrap against yet.

The ECIES call sites targeted by plan 69-09 (`inode.rs`, `replay.rs`, `content_ops.rs`) are also reached from ~9 other `crates/fuse` files not listed in that plan's scope: `fs.rs`, `read_ops.rs`, `dir_ops.rs`, `cache.rs`, `events.rs`, `poll.rs`, `operations.rs`, and 3 `platform/windows/*.rs` files.
`crates/sdk/src/lib.rs` is a shared edit point for multiple plans (69-06 and 69-08), forcing intra-wave serialization to avoid merge conflicts.

code.finding: `rotate_one` takes `parent_read_key: &[u8]` as a borrow (not owned) — the Rust type system itself, not just convention, prevents the function from zeroing the caller's key buffer, enforcing the terminal-owner zeroization invariant.

Cold-child rotation gating must source `generation`/`version_floor` from the parent `SealedChildRef` mirror, never from the child's own `PublishedNode.generation` (Pitfall 4/M1) — verified by a dedicated unit test that fails if the source is swapped.

`verify_subtree_clean`'s dirty-frontier check is generation-comparison based and, inherited unchanged from the TS reference, cannot detect a child that never individually rotated at all — a documented scope limitation.

workflow: GSD role-separation: when recovering from a planner crash, spawn a fresh single-plan `gsd-planner` for just the missing plan rather than authoring it inline as the orchestrator.

Canary-first pattern for unattended parallel execution: run the first plan of Wave 1 synchronously to validate the full executor→worktree→merge→cargo-gate pipeline before fanning out later waves in parallel.
Writing a durable handoff file to the scratchpad before a scheduled pause (ScheduleWakeup) preserves full recovery state even if context gets summarized across the gap.

Requirement-coverage gates (§13) require the actual requirement ID (e.g. `TEST-03`) in a plan's `requirements:` frontmatter — internal pseudo-IDs like `SC-01..SC-06` don't satisfy the gate even if they map conceptually.

Worktree agents' self-reported `expected_base` in `<worktree_metadata>` can be mis-captured (e.g. the agent's own docs commit instead of the true fork point) — always verify the actual merge-base via git before recording/merging.

When one plan in a wave uncovers a scope-invalidating finding (Rule 4 architectural change), correctly executed sibling plans that are independent (different crate, no shared dependency) can still be merged safely while the blocked one is held back.

friction: The gsd-planner agent hit an API error (connection closed mid-response) while writing the final plan (69-14), requiring a scheduled pause/resume recovery flow instead of a clean single pass.
Repeated false-negative `commit_failed` reports from the commit helper required manual git-log verification at multiple points (VALIDATION.md, plan commits, wave commits).
69-06's worktree metadata reported an incorrect `expected_base` (its own docs commit), requiring an extra manual git verification step before merging to avoid a bad merge.
Every fresh worktree lacked `node_modules`, causing husky pre-commit failures that each executor agent had to work around individually with `pnpm install`.

Plan 69-09's `files_modified` scope was incomplete relative to the actual codebase — the executor had to do investigative work mid-execution to discover the gap, rather than the planner catching it, burning a ~35 minute agent run that produced only partial output.
Discovering the architectural gap in 69-09 forced halting the entire FUSE-cutover portion of execution (invalidating 69-10 too), stalling wave 4/7 onward pending human replanning.
open_items: Plan 69-09 only partially executed (SC#6 CI grep gate landed); the ECIES→symmetric FUSE read-path swap is deferred pending a replan that also covers the ~9 additional `crates/fuse` files and the entire write path.
Plan 69-10 (D-04 legacy-type clean cutover) is now known to be invalid as scoped — it assumes the read path was fully migrated off legacy types, which is false — needs replanning before it can run.
Plans 69-12, 69-13, 69-14 (waves 5-7, including the WinFsp/Windows human-verify plan) have not yet been executed.
The SC#6 grep-gate added in 69-06/69-09 uses a placeholder symbol name that still needs confirming against the real crate-private resolve symbol at build/execution time.
The FUSE write path (mkdir/upload/delete/rename) needs to be migrated to Node v3/SealedChildRef symmetric sealing — identified as the root architectural gap blocking further cutover work.
User needs to decide on a replan approach for the remainder of Phase 69 execution before work can continue past wave 4.
